one_liner: C++20 IDNA to_ascii/to_unicode (UTS #46) domain-name encoder, about 1.26x faster than ICU.
what_it_does: Implements the WHATWG/UTS #46 domain-to-ASCII and domain-to-Unicode algorithms used to normalize internationalized domain names inside URL hosts (e.g. "me\u00dfagefactory.ca" -> "xn--meagefactory-m9a.ca"). The API is free functions over std::string_view/std::string, either returning a std::string (empty on error) or writing into an out-parameter and returning bool; it is not a drop-in replacement for ICU's uidna_openUTS46/uidna_nameToASCII_UTF8 C API. Ships as a normal CMake source library or, via singleheader/amalgamate.py, as an amalgamated single header+cpp pair for source-drop vendoring.
how_it_is_fast: An all-ASCII fast path (from_ascii_to_ascii) skips the whole Unicode pipeline and just lowercases in place. Non-ASCII input goes through a single UTF-8->UTF-32 transcode into a pre-sized buffer, a mapping pass into an exactly-sized second buffer to avoid reallocation, and an is_already_nfc check that skips NFC normalization entirely when the input is already normalized; labels are then walked with a single pointer scan instead of repeated string::find calls. Unicode/IDNA lookup tables are stored DEFLATE-compressed on disk and inflated once, lazily, behind an atomic-CAS/spin-wait (no mutex) into the same O(1) multi-stage lookup layout used pre-compression, so steady-state lookups are plain table hits and only first use pays an inflate cost.
when_to_use: Already building or embedding a URL/host-normalization layer and want IDNA to_ascii/to_unicode without linking full ICU
Workload is many small domain-name labels (matches the benchmark's label-oriented shape), not bulk text
Want to vendor a small, dual Apache-2.0/MIT-licensed source-drop instead of a system Unicode dependency
Building something with precedent for this exact use, e.g. Node.js or a ClickHouse-style URL/host column
when_not_to_use: Need general-purpose UTF-8 validation or transcoding, not domain-name IDNA specifically (out of scope for this library)
Need ICU's broader Unicode services (locale, collation, etc.) beyond IDNA
Want strong benchmark confidence: only one README micro-benchmark over 6 fixed sample domain strings, ICU version unstated, and the measured gain is modest (~1.26x)
Want a library with a long track record; only 69 stars and comparatively young/niche despite active maintenance

integration.dependencies: none for the core library; optional simdutf for UTF transcoding via ADA_USE_SIMDUTF (off by default); benchmarks/tests pull Google Benchmark, GoogleTest, and simdjson via CPM but are not needed to use the library
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 (GCC 12+, LLVM/Clang 12+, MSVC 2022 per README); note the singleheader demo.cpp is documented as compiled with -std=c++17, but the library core itself requires C++20
integration.platforms: portable C++20, no SIMD/arch requirement in the core path; explicit byte-swap code in table_store.hpp for big-endian platforms (e.g. s390x)
integration.thread_safety: table initialization is thread-safe via atomic CAS + spin-wait, no mutex (table_store.hpp); ensure_tables() returns false on init failure (OOM/corrupt blob), which callers must treat as a hard error; otherwise not documented beyond that
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — different API shape than ICU: std::string_view free functions vs ICU's uidna_openUTS46/uidna_nameToASCII_UTF8 C API, so a small wrapper is needed to substitute it

gotchas: to_ascii/to_unicode may accept or even produce invalid domains by design (documented WHATWG carve-outs), not strict RFC validity enforcement
Inputs over max_domain_input_bytes (16384 bytes) are rejected outright rather than truncated
Two API shapes exist: the value-returning to_ascii() has an ambiguous empty-string-on-error case; the bool-returning out-parameter overload avoids that ambiguity
Table inflate happens lazily on first call; a corrupted/OOM init path is a hard error per the source comments, not a silent fallback
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The catalogued siblings (simdutf8, xutf, SimdUnicode, utf8_range, encoding_rs, Boost.Text, unicode-transforms, etc.) are general UTF-8/Unicode validators or transcoders and don't do domain-name IDNA at all. Pick ada-url/idna specifically for URL host normalization (to_ascii/to_unicode), not as a substitute for those general-purpose libraries.
verified_claims_summary: On Apple M1 Max with LLVM 14 (C++20, Release build via the repo's own CMake benchmark target), Google Benchmark's to_ascii tool measured Ada at 1504 ns/op (48.5 M/s, ~3.99 M domains/s) versus ICU's uidna_nameToASCII_UTF8 at 1898 ns/op (38.5 M/s, ~3.16 M domains/s), over a fixed set of 6 sample domain strings defined in benchmarks/to_ascii.cpp — about 1.26x faster.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-08-24, 5 open issues, used by Node.js and referenced in a ClickHouse PR); dual Apache-2.0/MIT licensed and small enough to vendor as a source-drop despite a modest 69-star footprint.
